rituals.name: SPACED ECHO
rituals.plain:
Same line, different spacing. Memory has preferences, apparently.
Repeat MOON twice back-to-back. Then say RIVER once, count 1–5, and say RIVER again. Wait five seconds and notice which word returns more readily.
One pair is massed; one pair is separated by distraction.
Don't rehearse either word during the final wait.

rituals.name: MOTION TRAIL

Let a moving image leave a trail. The scene is doodling behind itself.
Run a short harmless mental motion. Let each previous position stay behind as a transparent ghost while the object keeps moving.
Old positions remain faintly visible.
Keep only the last four ghost positions.

Separate 'feels familiar' from 'was actually presented.'

rituals.name: EVENT-BOUNDARY CUT
rituals.plain:
Where does one remembered event become another? Memory has scene changes.
Recall a mild recent sequence and locate the first clear shift in place, goal or activity—such as leaving the car and entering the shop. Treat that shift as the event boundary.
Use a real context change, not an arbitrary time length.
Don't replay details on both sides once the boundary is found.

All doors stay unopened.

rituals.name: FUTURE CHECKSUM

Keep event, evidence, and next decision; discard the movie around them.
Try to rebuild the original worry using only those three slots.

rituals.name: MAX-INFO QUESTION
rituals.plain:
Which question would divide the possibilities best? Curiosity can aim before firing.
Imagine eight possible cards numbered 1–8. Compare asking 'Is it even?' with 'Is it greater than 7?' Decide which question would eliminate more possibilities regardless of the answer.
Prefer the split nearest 50/50.
Judge the split, not which answer you hope for.

rituals.name: REALITY PARTNER
rituals.plain:
SUPPORT FIRST
REALITY PARTNER

WHAT'S HAPPENING
[USER THOUGHT]

DO NOW
Prepare one concrete question about what is happening and verify it with someone you trust or a clinician.

NEXT
Keep decisions slow until checked.

WHY THIS MATTERS
A real-world verification channel replaces solitary certainty loops.

REMEMBER
A frightening interpretation that is hard to verify belongs in shared reality with another person.

SAFETY
This is not a solo reality test. Keep frightening or hard-to-verify interpretations unacted-on until a trusted person or clinician has helped check what is happening.
